goal: Distinguish data-only, PoE and PoE+ ports, then connect every supplied device within the switch budget.
context: Builds on wired devices and interface/cable inspection. The equipment and budgets are supplied; no electrical measurements or real hardware are needed.

concepts.title: A data connection is not a power supply
concepts.text: An Ethernet cable can carry data and, with compatible equipment, electrical power. PoE means Power over Ethernet. The switch is the power source; the phone, access point or camera is the powered device. A data-only port cannot power these supplied devices.

concepts.title: Match the device to the source port
concepts.text: Each supplied device has a power class. In this activity, class 4 needs a 30 W source reservation and a PoE+ port. Ordinary PoE ports provide up to 15.4 W; PoE+ provides up to 30 W. A different port may solve a source mismatch. Changing a checkbox cannot add hardware to a data-only port.

concepts.title: A reservation is not measured consumption
concepts.text: The supplied classes reserve 4 W (class 1), 7 W (class 2), 15.4 W (class 0 or 3) or 30 W (class 4) from the source. A 30 W-capable port does not always reserve 30 W: its connected device’s class decides the allocation. These are source reservations, not delivered power after cable losses or real-time consumption.

concepts.title: Several ports share one power budget
concepts.text: Add the reservations for powered devices and compare that total with the switch budget. An enabled, unused port reserves nothing in this model. Ports reserve in their listed order here; that is a teaching rule, not a claim about every switch. A capable port can still be denied when earlier reservations leave too little.

concepts.title: Use the controls to inspect a cause
concepts.text: Connect to chooses a supplied port for each device. A port accepts one cable, so choose Disconnected before reusing an occupied port. PoE enabled controls power on each capable port. Current power shows what the model actually allocates; Check power plan evaluates the full requirements after your final edit.

worked.label: Training AP · class 4
worked.explanation: A 15.4 W PoE source is too small, even if the whole switch has spare power.

worked.label: Helpdesk phone · class 1
worked.explanation: Any supplied compatible source can power the phone. A larger per-port maximum does not change its declared reservation.

worked.label: Entry camera · class 2
worked.explanation: The first example powers all three devices.

worked.label: Expected source total
worked.explanation: Count device allocations, not the sum of every port’s maximum. This example uses different equipment and values from your assignment.

worked.label: What a repair changes
worked.explanation: Choose a compatible unused port, inspect Current power and then Check example.

practice.title: Match each device to a port
practice.action: In Connect to, inspect the AP’s selected source. Choose Disconnected for a device before reusing its occupied port; connect the AP to a supplied PoE+ port. Inspect PoE enabled for that port.
practice.observe: Current power distinguishes an incompatible source, power disabled and an actual powered allocation. The port list describes hardware capacity; the power controls do not change that capacity.

practice.title: Inspect the reservations
practice.action: Compare the declared class reservations with the shared budget. Give the phone and camera their own compatible ports.
practice.observe: The source total changes when a powered device connects or loses power. The three expected reservations total 41 W.

practice.title: Check, break and retry
practice.action: Select Check example. Turn PoE enabled off for a required device, inspect its cause and check again. Restore a compatible powered connection and recheck.
practice.observe: Each result names the device and explains its cause. An edit clears the previous check, so a successful configuration cannot keep stale success after you break it.

requirements: Give Staff AP, Support phone and Camera powered connections using compatible supplied ports.
Connect each device to one distinct port and keep all supplied equipment.
Keep source reservations within the displayed shared switch budget.

concepts.text: When a device is out of service, disconnect it or turn off PoE on its port. Leaving it denied by an exhausted budget is a fault, not retirement. Preserve power to the required phone and access point; a power result alone does not test IP connectivity.
